facts.statement: The genus Phoebodus was first described by St. John and Worthen in 1875.
Phoebodus is classified as a genus containing multiple species.
Phoebodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish.
Phoebodus is placed in the extinct family Phoebodontidae.
Phoebodus lived during the middle to late Devonian periods and is found worldwide.
facts.quote: known from over a dozen species found worldwide spanning the middle to late Devonian

facts.statement: The time range for Phoebodus spans from the Givetian to the Norian, approximately 387.95 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Givetian to Norian (387.95 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Most species of Phoebodus are known only from isolated tricuspid teeth.
facts.quote: Most species are only known from their isolated tricuspid teeth

facts.statement: The teeth of Phoebodus are morphologically similar to those of frilled sharks and designed for grasping prey.
facts.quote: The teeth of Phoebodus and frilled sharks are also morphologically similar, and are designed for grasping prey

facts.statement: Phoebodus likely consumed small prey items that could be swallowed whole.
facts.quote: Phoebodus probably consumed small prey items that were capable of being swallowed whole

facts.statement: Representatives of the genus Phoebodus were certainly predatory animals, given the sharp morphology of their teeth.
facts.quote: Los representantes del género Phoebodus eran sin duda animales depredadores, dada la afilada morfología de sus dientes

facts.statement: The long body of Phoebodus saidelachus suggests it may have been a slow hunter that swallowed prey whole and held it with numerous three-pointed teeth.
facts.quote: El largo cuerpo de Phoebodus saidelachus indica que esta especie quizás era un cazador lento, que tragaba a sus presas enteras y las sujetaba con sus numerosos dientes de tres puntas

facts.statement: New fossil material of Phoebodus saidselachus was described from the Devonian strata of eastern Anti-Atlas, Morocco, by Klug et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: New fossil material of Phoebodus saidselachus, providing new information on the anatomy of members of this species, is described from the Devonian (Famennian) strata from eastern Anti-Atlas (Morocco) by Klug et al. (2026)

facts.statement: It is unclear exactly how Phoebodus hunted or what specific prey it consumed.
facts.quote: pero no está claro cómo cazaban ni de qué presas se alimentaban

facts.statement: The species Phoebodus brodiei and Phoebodus keuperinus are now placed in the genus Keuperodus in the family Jalodontidae.
facts.quote: Las especies de Phoebodus brodiei y Phoebodus keuperinus ahora se ubican en el género Keuperodus en la familia Jalodontidae
